item.title: 1972: The World Champion Oakland Athletics Acquire Centerfielder Bill North
item.description: The world champion Oakland Athletics acquire centerfielder Bill North from the Chicago Cubs for relief pitcher Bob Locker. North will be a key part of Oakland's 1973 and 1974 teams that win American League pennants and World Series titles, and he will lead the AL twice in stolen bases. Photo: John Morgan: Flickr, website, Facebook, Twitter, Instagram (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2019: The 2020 Season Was the First Under New Owner John Sherman
item.description: The 2020 season was the first under new owner John Sherman, whose purchase of the team was approved by MLB on November 21, 2019.

item.title: 2017: Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred Announced the Findings
item.description: On November 21, 2017, Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred announced the findings of the MLB investigation into Atlanta's international signings.

item.title: 2011: Seattle Mariners OF Greg Halman Is Found Fatally Stabbed
item.description: Seattle Mariners OF Greg Halman is found fatally stabbed in an apartment in Rotterdam. Photo: MoiraMoira (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2010: Kansas City Royals Pitcher Anthony Lerew Hurls a No-Hitter
item.description: Kansas City Royals pitcher Anthony Lerew hurls a no-hitter in the Venezuelan Winter League as the Navegantes de Magallanes blank the Leones del Caracas, 6–0. Lerew walks four and strikes out four, improving to 3–0 and a 1.11 ERA in six appearances. This is only the 16th no-hitter in the 66 years of history of the league. Photo: RCSmith84 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2004: The Team's Management Chose the Name "Washington Nationals"
item.description: On November 21, 2004, the team's management chose the name "Washington Nationals", revealing the club's official colors of red, white, and blue the next day. Photo: Hastings, George H., fl. 1885-1896, photographer. (Public domain).

item.title: 1989: Kevin Mitchell, Who Batted .291, Scored 100 Runs
item.description: Kevin Mitchell, who batted .291, scored 100 runs and led the San Francisco Giants to their first World Series appearance since 1962, is named National League MVP. Mitchell receives 20 of the 24 first-place votes. Photo: flickr user slgckgc (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1988: Carl Hubbell, 85, "The Meal Ticket," Hall-of-Fame Pitcher Who Won 253
item.description: Carl Hubbell, 85, "The Meal Ticket," Hall-of-Fame pitcher who won 253 games for the 1928–1943 New York Giants, then second-most among NL left-handers; named NL's MVP in 1933 and 1936, he led league in wins and ERA three times each and had 1.79 ERA in six World Series starts; his 1,677 strikeouts were NL record for portsiders until 1958, and he won 24 straight games in 1936–1937; in 1934 MLB All-Star Game, he fanned… Photo: AP (Public domain).

item.title: 1978: The New York Yankees Sign Free-Agent Left-Hander Tommy John
item.description: The New York Yankees sign free-agent left-hander Tommy John, formerly with the Los Angeles Dodgers. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1970: New York Mets Outfielder Tommie Agee Becomes the First Non-Pitcher
item.description: New York Mets outfielder Tommie Agee becomes the first non-pitcher to win a Gold Glove in both leagues. Agee also won the honor with the Chicago White Sox during his 1966 rookie of the year season. Photo: Bernard Gotfryd (Public domain).

item.title: 1969: The Cleveland Indians Send José Cardenal to the St. Louis Cardinals
item.description: The Cleveland Indians send José Cardenal to the St. Louis Cardinals for fellow outfielder Vada Pinson. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1968: The Cincinnati Reds Trade Shortstop Leo Cárdenas
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds trade shortstop Leo Cárdenas, a four-time NL All-Star, to the Minnesota Twins for left-hander Jim Merritt. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1967: Ohio's Big-League Clubs Make an Interleague Trade When the Cleveland
item.description: Ohio's big-league clubs make an interleague trade when the Cleveland Indians obtain outfielder Tommy Harper from the Cincinnati Reds for pitcher George Culver, first baseman Fred Whitfield and outfielder Bob Raudman. Photo: Boston Red Sox (Public domain).

item.title: 1967: Harper Was Traded to the Cleveland Indians in Exchange for George
item.description: On November 21, 1967, Harper was traded to the Cleveland Indians in exchange for George Culver, Bob Raudman and Fred Whitfield. Photo: Boston Red Sox (Public domain).

item.title: 1962: Always in Search of Right-Handed Power
item.description: Always in search of right-handed power, the Boston Red Sox acquire slugging first baseman Dick Stuart from the Pittsburgh Pirates, along with relief pitcher Jack Lamabe, for pitcher Don Schwall (1961's AL Rookie of the Year) and 25-year-old catcher Jim Pagliaroni. Stuart, 30, will live up to his reputation for home-run power and terrible defensive play during his two seasons in Boston. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1959: Gernert Was Involved in the First Interleague Trade Without Waivers
item.description: Gernert was involved in the first interleague trade without waivers in baseball history, on November 21, 1959, when Boston shipped him to the Cubs for first baseman Jim Marshall and pitcher Dave Hillman. Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1959: In the First Inter-League Trade Without Waivers
item.description: In the first inter-league trade without waivers, the NL Chicago Cubs send first baseman Jim Marshall and pitcher Dave Hillman to the AL Boston Red Sox in exchange for first baseman Dick Gernert. Also today, the Kansas City Athletics deal catcher Frank House to the Cincinnati Reds for pitcher Tom Acker. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1958: Mel Ott, 49, Hall of Fame Right Fielder
item.description: Mel Ott, 49, Hall of Fame right fielder and 12-time All-Star who played his 22-season big league career with the New York Giants from 1926 to 1947; jumped from his high school team into the majors as a 17-year-old, and a member of Giants' 1933 World Series champions; led the National League in home runs and walks six times, in runs scored, triples and outfield double plays twice, and in runs batted in once, ending… Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1955: Carl Stotz, Principal Founding Father of the Little League
item.description: Carl Stotz, principal founding father of the Little League, sues the organization for breach of contract. The suit will be settled out of court.

item.title: 1952: Joe Black, Who Posted a 15–4 Record, 2.15 Earned Run Average
item.description: Joe Black, who posted a 15–4 record, 2.15 earned run average, and 15 saves for the pennant-winning Brooklyn Dodgers, wins the National League Rookie of the Year Award. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1949: Bill Veeck Sells the Cleveland Indians for $2.2 Million to a Local
item.description: Bill Veeck sells the Cleveland Indians for $2.2 million to a local syndicate headed by Ellis Ryan. Hank Greenberg will be the new general manager. Photo: US Marine Corps (Public domain).

item.title: 1934: The New York Yankees Acquire Joe DiMaggio From San Francisco
item.description: The New York Yankees acquire Joe DiMaggio from San Francisco of the Pacific Coast League. Photo: Tom Sande (Public domain).

item.title: 1933: Klein Was Traded to the Cubs for $65,000 (Equivalent to $1,616,645
item.description: On November 21, 1933, Klein was traded to the Cubs for $65,000 (equivalent to $1,616,645 in 2025) and three other players, Klein hit 20 and 21 home runs in his two full seasons with the Cubs (1934, 1935) and batted . Photo: Goudey Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1933: Philadelphia Phillies Right Fielder Chuck Klein
item.description: Philadelphia Phillies right fielder Chuck Klein, who won the National League Triple Crown after hitting .368 with 28 home runs and 120 RBI, is sold to the Cubs for $125,000 and three players. Klein, who also led the NL in hits (223), doubles (44), extra bases (79), total bases (365), slugging (.602), on-base % (.422) and OPS (1.025), and finished second in runs (102) and fourth in stolen bases (15), is the only… Photo: Goudey Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1893: Ban Johnson Is Named President, Secretary
item.description: Ban Johnson is named president, secretary, and treasurer of the recently reorganized Western League. Under Johnson's leadership the WL will prosper. Photo: No known restrictions on publication (Public domain).

item.title: 1889: The National League Issues Its Reply to the Players' League
item.description: The National League issues its reply to the Players' League manifesto. Claiming that the League saved baseball in 1876 and that under the reserve rules players' salaries had "more than trebled", the NL denounces the Brotherhood movement as "the efforts of certain overpaid players to again control [baseball] for their own aggrandizement. . . to its ultimate dishonor and disintegration." Photo: Betz, John Jr (Public domain).

item.title: 1888: The National League Formally Admits the Cleveland Blues
item.description: The National League formally admits the Cleveland Blues from the American Association. The Blues are the second team to leave the AA for the NL, following the Pittsburgh Alleghenys who made the switch after the 1886 season. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1887: In the American Association, the St. Louis Browns Announce a Trade
item.description: In the American Association, the St. Louis Browns announce a trade that ships Bill Gleason and Curt Welch to the Philadelphia Athletics in exchange for Fred Mann, Chippy McGarr, and Jocko Milligan, plus $3,000. This is the first of a significant number of trades or sales in the majors, mostly to the Brooklyn Grays. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
